findings.source_quote: In the mid-1600s, the local Prince, Elector Ludwig, invited the exiled Swiss Brethren into the Palatinate to help rebuild the farms...
findings.suggested_fix: Translate the title accurately. Replace "Mfalme mteule Ludwig" with a phrase that conveys Elector rather than king (e.g., "Waziri Mfalme mteule/Alimkaribia Mfalme mteule" is incorrect). Use a Kiswahili phrase such as "Mfalme mteule (Elector) Ludwig" or better: "Mfalme mteule (Elector) Ludwig" is still confusing—recommended: "Mchaguzi (Elector) Ludwig" or "Ludwig, Mchaguzi (Elector)" so the historical office 'Elector' is preserved. Maintain the name order and keep the original historical term in parentheses if helpful: "Mchaguzi (Elector) Ludwig".
findings.translation_quote: Katikati za miaka ya 1600, Mkuu wa eneo hilo, Mfalme mteule Ludwig, alimkaribisha Wabrethreni waliotawanywa katika Pfaltzland ili kusaidia...

findings.location: Paragraph about Germantown (sentence: "It seems that here is where the Swiss Brethren first became known as Mennists or Mennonites.")
findings.source_quote: It seems that here is where the Swiss Brethren first became known as Mennists or Mennonites.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the mixed-language term. Replace "Mennists au Mennonites" with a Kiswahili rendering such as "Mennists au Mennonites" is mixing French; use "Mennists au" -> "Mennists au" should be fully Kiswahili/English: e.g., "walianza kuitwa Mennists au Mennonites" or better simply "walipoanza kuitwa Mennonites (Mennists)". Ensure only Kiswahili words or conventional names remain.
findings.translation_quote: Inaonekana hapa ndipo Wabrethreni wa Uswisi walipoanza kuitwa Mennists au Mennonites.
